# taylor_impact_2d — reference sensitivities (ADR-0076)

Sensitivity of each quantity of interest to `impact_velocity_m_s`, taken by central differences across the neighbouring cases of the sweep (one-sided at the ends of a line). Each value carries two error terms: *trunc*, the same difference at twice the step (three times the leading error of a central difference; an estimate, not a bound), and *meas*, the quantity's declared noise propagated through the difference. A point is **judged** when the larger term is at most 0.5 of the sensitivity and enters a model's pooled headline; otherwise it is *reported* (shown in italics) and a model's number there is read against an uncertain reference. Nothing here is fitted to the data.

## Declared noise

| Quantity | σ absolute | σ relative | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| `final_length` | 0.5 | 0 | an extent read from particle centres is uncertain by about one SPH lattice spacing, 0.5 mm at the benchmark resolution |
| `mushroom_width` | 0.5 | 0 | as final_length: one lattice spacing, 0.5 mm |
| `peak_von_mises` | 0 | 0.01 | the card declares a particle-scale floor of ~0.12 relative L2 on the von Mises field; the particle mean averages that jitter down, and 1 % of the peak is declared as a conservative stand-in until the convergence case is measured |
| `t_peak_von_mises` | 0.002 | 0 | the time of a peak is read at the 2 µs output interval; one interval is the least it can be wrong by |
